Superb Curry Restaurant Built with Heart and Soul
May 2025 • Friends
There’s something special about walking into a new restaurant where the team’s heart is on full display—and Curry-licious is exactly that. Bursting with all the enthusiasm and soul of a passionate start-up, this place delivers not just food, but warmth and promise.

I ordered the butter chicken, a personal go-to, and it exceeded every expectation. I lean towards milder, richer curries, and this was everything I hoped for and more. The creamy texture was beautifully balanced with tangy tomato notes and a blend of fragrant spices that lingered just enough to keep each bite interesting. This is comfort food at its finest—the kind of meal that restores and delights.

Offered a traditional dessert inspired by Delhi—a blend of rice, coconut, condensed milk, cardamom, and saffron—I accepted without hesitation. The result was a creamy, smooth creation, delicately sweet and infused with spice. A perfect ending to the evening.

The drink selection is solid, catering to a range of tastes, and the overall setting makes it a superb place for a night out with friends. 
.
I sincerely wish Curry-licious all the success it deserves. With food like this—and heart to match—it’s well on its way.

"Currylucious Has Potential – A Few Suggestions for Growth"
Jun 2025 • Friends
My friends and I—five of us—visited Currylucious yesterday during our first trip to Ho Chi Minh City, after searching for Indian food options online. The place caught our attention with its impressive 4.9 rating and positive reviews on Google.

Upon arriving, we found the ambience to be modest with limited seating. However, the owner—an Indian who has lived in Ho Chi Minh City for the past seven years and recently opened the restaurant two months ago—warmly welcomed us and guided us to a table himself.

We placed a fairly large order:

Green salad

Chicken Manchow Soup

Chicken Tikka Kebab

Kali Mirch Kebab

Prawns Koliwada

Kadai Chicken

Chicken Tikka Masala (gravy)

5 Tandoori rotis

1 Fresh lime soda (sweet-salty)

4 Cokes

The owner informed us that the food would take around 8–10 minutes to arrive, which we appreciated. However, we were surprised he didn’t write down the order, considering its length.

After about 20 minutes, the first item to arrive was the Kali Mirch Kebab instead of the soup. Normally, soup is served first, so this was unexpected. About 10 minutes later, we received a Fish Kebab, which we never ordered—we had ordered Prawns Koliwada. Despite the error, we decided to go with the flow, considering it’s a new establishment.

Next, we received another plate of Kali Mirch Kebab, which again was not part of our original order. The dish was dry and lacked flavor. The Fish Kebab, too, didn’t meet expectations. When we inquired about the soup, the owner asked whether we had ordered veg or non-veg—by then we had lost patience and told him to cancel it.

Later, we were served Chicken Tikka Masala Kebab, which was undercooked and unappetizing. The gravies—Kadai Chicken and Chicken Tikka Masala—arrived together and oddly tasted the same, more like a basic vegetable curry than distinct chicken dishes. The rotis were average.

Surprisingly, we were again served Chicken Tikka Masala Kebab, which we hadn’t ordered (again), but accepted it out of courtesy. Toward the end, we ordered Chicken Egg Fried Rice, which came with beans—an unusual addition—and it tasted average.

The total bill came to approximately ₹5,000 INR, and the owner extended a 10% discount as an acknowledgment of the service and order issues.

I’ve written this detailed review not to discourage the restaurant or its owner, but to offer constructive feedback. The most critical mistake was not writing down the order, which led to confusion and mismanagement. Given that this is a new venture, the owner should focus on:

1. Accurately recording orders

2. Improving kitchen coordination and reducing wait times

3. Enhancing the taste, texture, and preparation quality of the food

If you're planning to visit Currylucious, I’d still encourage you to try it and support a new entrepreneur, but I’d recommend having a clear conversation about your order upfront to avoid similar issues.

Craving Indian food abroad? This place nailed it
May 2025 • Friends
This place is located at an excellent spot. I was traveling through Vietnam for a couple of weeks, and no matter how comfortable you are with Western food, your Indian soul eventually starts craving that familiar, authentic taste. And boy—what a lucky find this was!

I was aimlessly strolling down Walking Street when I stumbled upon this restaurant. Butter chicken and naan are my staples, and honestly, after trying naan at several other places—even in different countries—I usually keep my expectations low. But this time, I was blown away. The naan here was better than most I’ve had in India—authentic, soft, and cooked to perfection. The butter chicken? Rich, flavourful, and comforting in every bite.

It was so good that I ended up coming back three more times during my short trip. The atmosphere, the vibe, and the service are all top-notch. The owner is a genuinely warm and welcoming person, which just adds to the experience.

Easily a 5/5.
